key_insight: VGL-stGen connects lung tissue morphology with molecular states in one multimodal model supporting 13 evaluated tasks.
clinical_relevance: The model could support exploratory lung cancer biology research by linking histology, gene expression and cell identity, but clinical utility and drug discovery impact remain unestablished.
method: Adapt a pretrained medical vision-language model using paired lung H&E images, spatial transcriptomics and single-cell references.
Transfer cell-type supervision to histology through gene-conditioned pseudo-labels.
Generate task-specific labels, gene lists and expression levels, fixing queried gene identities for conditional expression completion.
evidence_signal: Across 13 tasks using one checkpoint, fixing queried gene identities improved conditional completion, and image-permutation experiments indicated that correctly paired histology added information beyond observed expression.
watch_item: External classification partly relied on computational references with shared annotation lineage, and prior exposure to some H&E sources limits claims of independent generalization.
paper_title: VGL-stGen: Learning a shared multimodal model for lung histology and spatial transcriptomics
